title: Claude Drop: housing-data_narrative
author: Claude
text:
A Louisiana minimum-wage worker would need about 121 hours of work a week to afford a two-bedroom at fair market rent in 2026

Louisiana has no state minimum wage, so $7.25 is the floor. At that pay, a two-bedroom takes three full-time jobs. Nobody should need three jobs for a roof.

Source: National Low Income Housing Coalition, Out of Reach 2026: Louisiana

title: Claude Drop: housing-data_narrative
author: Claude
text:
The 2026 two-bedroom housing wage in the New Orleans-Metairie metro is $25.60 an hour

The people who cook, clean and play music for the tourism economy often can't afford the city they power. A city that runs on hospitality should be hospitable to its workers.

Source: National Low Income Housing Coalition, Out of Reach 2026: Louisiana

title: Claude Drop: housing-data_narrative
author: Claude
text:
There was a shortage of 7.2 million affordable and available rental homes for extremely low-income renters in 2026's analysis

Only 35 affordable homes exist for every 100 of the lowest-income renter households. The market doesn't build for people at the bottom. Public housing must.

Source: National Low Income Housing Coalition, The Gap 2026

title: Claude Drop: housing-data_narrative
author: Claude
text:
74% of extremely low-income renter households were severely cost-burdened, paying more than half their income for housing

Three out of four of the poorest renters spend over half their income just on shelter. One car repair or sick day and they're facing eviction.

Source: National Low Income Housing Coalition, The Gap 2026

title: Claude Drop: housing-data_narrative
author: Claude
text:
The national home price-to-income ratio reached 5.0 in 2024, versus about 3.2 throughout the 1990s

A typical home now costs five years of household income. A generation ago it was about three. Same houses. Bigger prices. Smaller chance for working families.

Source: Harvard Joint Center for Housing Studies, 2025

title: Claude Drop: housing-data_narrative
author: Claude
text:
From 2019 to 2024, U.S. median single-family home prices rose 48% while median household income rose 22%

Prices more than doubled income growth in five years. That's why saving for a down payment feels like running up a down escalator.

Source: Harvard Joint Center for Housing Studies, 2025

title: Claude Drop: housing-data_narrative
author: Claude
text:
The median age of first-time homebuyers hit a record 40 in 2025

First-time buyers also fell to a record-low 21% of purchases. Homeownership used to start a family's journey. Now it starts in middle age, if at all.

Source: National Association of Realtors, 2025 Profile of Home Buyers and Sellers

title: Claude Drop: housing-data_narrative
author: Claude
text:
The homeownership rate for white non-Hispanic households was 74.5% versus 45.4% for Black households in the second quarter of 2026

A 29-point gap. It was built by redlining, exclusion and unequal lending. What law built, law can unbuild: down payment help, fair lending enforcement, public housing that builds equity.

Source: U.S. Census Bureau, Housing Vacancies and Homeownership, Q2 2026

title: Claude Drop: housing-data_narrative
author: Claude
text:
Only 35.2% of households headed by someone under 35 owned their home in the second quarter of 2026

Young families are renting longer and paying more. Every year locked out is a year without building wealth.

Source: U.S. Census Bureau, Housing Vacancies and Homeownership, Q2 2026

title: Claude Drop: housing-data_narrative
author: Claude
text:
Investors, defined as buyers owning three or more properties, made about 29% to 32% of U.S. home purchases in the first half of 2025

Nearly a third of homes went to investors. Most were small investors; large ones were about 3% of buys. Either way, families bidding against cash buyers lose.

Source: Cotality Investor Purchase Indicator, 2025

title: Claude Drop: housing-data_narrative
author: Claude
text:
Build-to-rent homes made up 11% of new single-family homes in 2025, nearly three times the historical average

More new houses are built never to be sold to a family. A permanent renter class is being poured in concrete.

Source: Harvard Joint Center for Housing Studies, State of the Nation's Housing 2026

title: Claude Drop: housing-data_narrative
author: Claude
text:
The Justice Department and several states sued RealPage in August 2024, alleging its software helped landlords coordinate rents; RealPage denied the allegations

DOJ alleged landlords fed private data into one algorithm that recommended rents. RealPage said it did nothing wrong. Whatever a court would have found, renters deserve rents set by competition, not a shared machine.

Source: U.S. Department of Justice, 2024

title: Claude Drop: housing-data_narrative
author: Claude
text:
RealPage settled the DOJ antitrust case in November 2025 without admitting wrongdoing or paying a penalty, agreeing to limits on its use of nonpublic landlord data

No fine, no admission, but new limits and oversight. A federal judge approved the deal in 2026. Tenants won rules. Now we need laws.

Source: U.S. Department of Justice; The Real Deal, 2025

title: Claude Drop: housing-data_narrative
author: Claude
text:
Greystar agreed in 2025 to a $7 million settlement with nine state attorneys general over algorithmic rent-setting and to stop using rivals' nonpublic data

The nation's largest property manager agreed to stop setting rents with competitors' private data. That's what pressure does.

Source: California Attorney General, 2025

title: Claude Drop: housing-data_narrative
author: Claude
text:
New York became the first state to ban algorithmic rent-setting software that uses competitors' data when the law was signed on October 16, 2025

Cities like San Francisco, Philadelphia, Seattle and Jersey City acted first. Then a whole state. Louisiana can follow.

Source: New York State, 2025

title: Claude Drop: housing-data_narrative
author: Claude
text:
Invitation Homes agreed in 2024 to pay $48 million to settle FTC charges over junk fees and unfair tenant practices

One of the largest single-family landlords settled without admitting wrongdoing. Hidden fees are a quiet rent increase. Ban them.

Source: Federal Trade Commission, 2024

title: Claude Drop: housing-data_narrative
author: Claude
text:
Eviction Lab tracked about 1.23 million eviction filings in 2025 across 48 sites holding roughly a third of U.S. renter households

That's just the places they can see. Across those sites, about one renter household in 13 faced an eviction case.

Source: Eviction Lab, Princeton University, 2025

title: Claude Drop: housing-data_narrative
author: Claude
text:
New Orleans had an eviction filing rate of about 8% of renter households in 2025

About 8 in every 100 renter households in New Orleans faced an eviction filing. A filing alone can scar a tenant's record for years.

Source: Eviction Lab, Princeton University, 2025

title: Claude Drop: housing-data_narrative
author: Claude
text:
About 83% of landlords have legal representation in eviction court, compared with about 4% of tenants nationally

One side brings a lawyer. The other brings a shoebox of receipts. That's not justice. That's an ambush.

Source: National Low Income Housing Coalition, Advocates' Guide 2026

title: Claude Drop: housing-data_narrative
author: Claude
text:
26 U.S. jurisdictions, including 5 states, 19 cities and 2 counties, had enacted a tenant right to counsel by 2026

Right to counsel started in New York City in 2017 and has spread. Tenant organizing won every one of those laws.

Source: National Low Income Housing Coalition, Advocates' Guide 2026

title: Claude Drop: housing-data_narrative
author: Claude
text:
New York City eviction filings fell from about 247,000 in 2013 to about 118,000 in 2024 after the city phased in a right to counsel

Lawyers changed the math. When landlords know a tenant will be represented, fewer weak cases get filed.

Source: New York City Comptroller, 2025

title: Claude Drop: housing-data_narrative
author: Claude
text:
HUD counted 230,366 people in families with children experiencing homelessness in January 2025

That's down 11% from 2024, which shows help works. It's still a small city of parents and kids without a home of their own.

Source: U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development, 2025 AHAR

title: Claude Drop: housing-data_narrative
author: Claude
text:
Black Americans made up 33% of people experiencing homelessness in 2025 but about 14% of the U.S. population

Homelessness follows the color line drawn by redlining, wage gaps and evictions. Housing justice is racial justice.

Source: U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development, 2025 AHAR

title: Claude Drop: housing-data_narrative
author: Claude
text:
About 13.8 million eligible low-income renter households received no federal rental assistance in 2023

Housing aid is not an entitlement. It's a lottery. Only about one in four who qualify get help.

Source: Harvard Joint Center for Housing Studies, State of the Nation's Housing 2026

title: Claude Drop: housing-data_narrative
author: Claude
text:
More than 2.8 million families were on housing voucher waiting lists and about 1.6 million on public housing lists in a national survey

And 48.4% of voucher waiting lists were closed to new applicants. Millions can't even get in line.

Source: Public and Affordable Housing Research Corporation, 2016 (survey data from 2012)

title: Claude Drop: housing-data_narrative
author: Claude
text:
The mortgage interest deduction is a tax expenditure of about $52.6 billion in 2025, claimed on about 17.8 million returns

Washington spends tens of billions a year helping people with mortgages, mostly through the tax code. Housing help for the comfortable is called a deduction. For the poor it's called welfare.

Source: Joint Committee on Taxation via Congressional Research Service, 2026

title: Claude Drop: housing-data_narrative
author: Claude
text:
Households with income over $200,000 receive about 78.2% of the mortgage interest deduction's benefit

Almost four of every five dollars go to the top. Over 96% goes to households above $100,000. Flip it to help first-time buyers and renters.

Source: Joint Committee on Taxation via Congressional Research Service, 2026

title: Claude Drop: housing-data_narrative
author: Claude
text:
There were about 883,877 public housing units in December 2024, down from a peak of about 1.1 million

HUD estimates about 10,000 public housing units are lost every year. We're shrinking the one housing program that truly houses the poorest.

Source: National Low Income Housing Coalition, Advocates' Guide 2025, citing HUD

title: Claude Drop: housing-data_narrative
author: Claude
text:
HUD estimated the public housing capital repair backlog at $50 billion or more in 2025

Leaky roofs and broken boilers didn't happen by accident. Congress underfunded repairs for decades, then blamed the buildings.

Source: National Low Income Housing Coalition, Advocates' Guide 2025, citing HUD (estimate)

title: Claude Drop: housing-data_narrative
author: Claude
text:
The 1998 Faircloth Amendment capped public housing units at the number each agency operated on October 1, 1999

Congress made it effectively illegal to grow the public housing stock. Repeal the cap and let housing authorities build.

Source: Quality Housing and Work Responsibility Act of 1998

title: Claude Drop: housing-data_narrative
author: Claude
text:
The City of Vienna owns about 220,000 municipal apartments, and about half of Viennese live in municipal or subsidized housing

Vienna treats housing as public infrastructure, like roads and water. Its social housing serves working and middle-class families alike.

Source: City of Vienna, Wiener Wohnen / socialhousing.wien

title: Claude Drop: housing-data_narrative
author: Claude
text:
In 2025, 77.2% of Singapore's resident households lived in public HDB flats and 91.2% owned their homes

Most of a nation housed by public construction. Different country, different system, same lesson: governments can build homes at scale.

Source: Singapore Department of Statistics, 2025

title: Claude Drop: housing-data_narrative
author: Claude
text:
Louisiana had the highest average homeowners insurance premium in the U.S. at the end of 2025, about $4,238 a year

That's on top of the mortgage. For many Louisiana families, insurance now costs more than property taxes. Some are being insured right out of their homes.

Source: Newrez analysis of mortgage servicing data, 2026 (industry estimate)

title: Claude Drop: housing-data_narrative
author: Claude
text:
Louisiana homeowners insurance rates rose an average of 16.2% in 2022 and 14% in 2023

Two years of double-digit hikes after Laura, Ida and a dozen insurer failures. Increases slowed to 6.6% in 2024 and 4.4% in 2025, but slower climbing is still climbing.

Source: Louisiana Department of Insurance, 2026 statement

title: Claude Drop: housing-data_narrative
author: Claude
text:
Average monthly U.S. home insurance premiums rose 72% from 2019 to 2025

Insurance is the fastest-growing piece of housing costs. Landlords pass it to tenants. Homeowners eat it. Climate risk is a housing cost now.

Source: Harvard Joint Center for Housing Studies, State of the Nation's Housing 2026

title: Claude Drop: housing-data_narrative
author: Claude
text:
48.4% of Louisiana renters were cost-burdened in 2023

Half of Louisiana's renters pay over 30% of income for housing. Of those, more than half pay over 50%. Every parish has neighbors in this squeeze.

Source: LSU Shreveport Center for Business and Economic Research, 2025 (2023 ACS data)

title: Claude Drop: housing-data_narrative
author: Claude
text:
Louisiana had 588,653 renter households, about 33% of all households, in NLIHC's 2026 analysis

One in three Louisiana households rents. That's a voting bloc bigger than many cities. Organized renters can swing a parish.

Source: National Low Income Housing Coalition, Out of Reach 2026: Louisiana

title: Claude Drop: housing-data_narrative
author: Claude
text:
New Orleans' 2023 ordinance limits residential short-term rentals to one per square block, awarded by lottery

In October 2025 the appeals court largely upheld the city's rules but struck its ban on business entities holding permits. Neighborhoods won most of the fight.

Source: New Orleans City Council, 2023; U.S. Fifth Circuit, 2025

title: Claude Drop: housing-data_narrative
author: Claude
text:
Minneapolis grew its housing stock 12% from 2017 to 2022 while rents rose 1%; the rest of Minnesota grew 4% with rents up 14%

When cities let homes get built, rents can steady. Zoning reform isn't the whole answer, but blocking homes is part of the problem.

Source: Pew Charitable Trusts, 2024

title: Claude Drop: housing-data_narrative
author: Claude
text:
San Francisco's 1994 rent control expansion made covered tenants nearly 20% more likely to stay at their address, while covered landlords cut rental supply 15%

Rent control protected people's homes. It also shrank supply and raised citywide rents about 5.1%. The lesson: stabilize rents and build public homes so supply doesn't shrink.

Source: Diamond, McQuade and Qian, NBER/Stanford, 2019

title: Claude Drop: housing-data_narrative
author: Claude
text:
Apartments renting for under $1,000 a month, adjusted for inflation, fell about 30% from 2014 to 2024

The low-rent apartment is disappearing. Meanwhile units over $2,000 doubled. The market builds for the top and lets the bottom vanish.

Source: Harvard Joint Center for Housing Studies, State of the Nation's Housing 2026

title: Claude Drop: housing-data_narrative
author: Claude
text:
U.S. asking rents for professionally managed apartments in early 2026 were 29% higher than in 2020

Rents dipped 0.5% over the year. Don't let anyone call that relief. The ceiling moved and stayed.

Source: Harvard Joint Center for Housing Studies, State of the Nation's Housing 2026

title: Claude Drop: housing-data_narrative
author: Claude
text:
The Census Bureau said in August 2026 that the 2025 American Community Survey 1-year release date was still being determined

The survey that measures rent burden for every parish was delayed by a new Commerce Department disclosure order. More than 100 organizations objected. Count us.

Source: U.S. Census Bureau, August 4, 2026

title: Claude Drop: housing-data_narrative
author: Claude
text:
72 million U.S. homes face at least a moderate risk of loss from climate-related disasters

In the Gulf South, housing policy is climate policy. Build higher, build stronger, and make insurance a public promise.

Source: Harvard Joint Center for Housing Studies, State of the Nation's Housing 2026 (using FEMA National Risk Index)

title: Claude Drop: housing-karl_voice
author: Claude
text:
How many renters are drowning in rent right now?

A record 22.7 million renter households paid more than 30% of their income for housing in 2024. That's 49% of all renters, Harvard's Joint Center for Housing Studies reports. Half the renters in America are one bad month from the edge. That isn't a personal failure. It's a system working as designed.

title: Claude Drop: housing-karl_voice
author: Claude
text:
What does a worker need to earn to rent a modest two-bedroom?

$34.73 an hour, full time, according to the National Low Income Housing Coalition's Out of Reach 2026. The average renter earns $24.84. That's a gap of almost $10 an hour, every hour, every week. The rent is out of reach because the pay is held down.

title: Claude Drop: housing-karl_voice
author: Claude
text:
What's the housing wage in Louisiana?

NLIHC says a Louisiana worker needs $21.88 an hour to afford a two-bedroom at fair market rent in 2026. In New Orleans it's $25.60. Our minimum wage is still the federal $7.25. At that wage you'd need about 121 hours a week. There are only 168 hours in a week.

title: Claude Drop: housing-karl_voice
author: Claude
text:
Is there really a shortage of affordable homes?

For the lowest-income renters, yes, and it's brutal. NLIHC's The Gap 2026 counts a shortage of 7.2 million affordable and available homes for extremely low-income renters. Only 35 homes for every 100 families who need one. That's musical chairs with 65 people left standing.

title: Claude Drop: housing-karl_voice
author: Claude
text:
Why do people say buying a house is impossible now?

Because the math broke. Harvard's Joint Center found the typical home cost 5 times the typical household income in 2024. In the 1990s it was about 3.2. From 2019 to 2024, home prices rose 48% while income rose 22%. Wages walked. Prices ran.

title: Claude Drop: housing-karl_voice
author: Claude
text:
How old is the typical first-time homebuyer now?

Forty. That's an all-time high in the National Association of Realtors' 2025 buyer profile. First-time buyers fell to a record-low 21% of purchases. Our parents bought at 29. We're told to wait until our kids are in middle school.

title: Claude Drop: housing-karl_voice
author: Claude
text:
Is the racial homeownership gap still real?

Yes. Census data for the second quarter of 2026: 74.5% of white non-Hispanic households own their home. Black households, 45.4%. Hispanic households, 48.1%. That gap was built by law, redlining and exclusion. It can be closed by law too.

title: Claude Drop: housing-karl_voice
author: Claude
text:
Are Wall Street investors buying up all the houses?

Investors bought nearly a third of homes sold in early 2025, Cotality found. But be precise. Cotality counts anyone owning three or more properties as an investor, and most are small ones. The giant firms were about 3% of purchases. The problem isn't just the big names. It's a market that treats a roof as a stock tip.

title: Claude Drop: housing-karl_voice
author: Claude
text:
What was the RealPage case about?

In August 2024 the Justice Department and several states sued RealPage, alleging its software let big landlords share private rent data and steer rents higher together. RealPage denied wrongdoing. In November 2025 it settled with DOJ: no admission, no fine, but limits on how its software uses landlords' private data, plus a monitor. A federal judge approved the deal in 2026. Greystar, the biggest property manager, separately agreed to stop using rival landlords' private data and paid $7 million to settle with nine states. Algorithm or not, coordinating rents is a choice.

title: Claude Drop: housing-karl_voice
author: Claude
text:
Did anyone actually ban rent-setting algorithms?

Yes. New York became the first state to ban algorithmic rent-setting that uses rivals' data when Governor Hochul signed the law in October 2025. San Francisco, Philadelphia, Seattle and Jersey City moved first. Tenants pushed. Lawmakers moved. That's how it works.

title: Claude Drop: housing-karl_voice
author: Claude
text:
How fast can you be evicted in Louisiana?

Fast. A Louisiana landlord can give five days' notice to vacate for unpaid rent, and many leases waive even that. After a judgment, a tenant can have about 24 hours to get out. Five days. One day. Your whole life on the curb. We need real tenant protections in this state.

title: Claude Drop: housing-karl_voice
author: Claude
text:
How common are evictions?

Eviction Lab tracked about 1.23 million eviction filings in 2025 in just the cities and states it monitors, which hold about a third of U.S. renters. In New Orleans the filing rate was about 8 renter households in 100. One in thirteen across tracked sites. Every filing is a family in crisis.

title: Claude Drop: housing-karl_voice
author: Claude
text:
Does right to counsel actually stop evictions?

Yes. New York City passed the first tenant right to counsel in 2017. City reports found 84% of tenants with a lawyer stayed in their homes in its first years. Filings fell from about 247,000 in 2013 to about 118,000 in 2024. Without that right, about 4% of tenants nationally have a lawyer. About 83% of landlords do. Level the room.

title: Claude Drop: housing-karl_voice
author: Claude
text:
Is homelessness about drugs and bad choices?

Look at who's counted. HUD's 2025 report counted 230,366 people in families with children. Black Americans are 14% of the population and 33% of the homeless count. Addiction is real and deserves treatment. But kids don't choose to be priced out. Rents do the evicting.

title: Claude Drop: housing-karl_voice
author: Claude
text:
How many people who qualify for housing help actually get it?

About one in four. NLIHC and Harvard's Joint Center both say so. In 2023 about 13.8 million eligible low-income renter households got no federal help at all. Imagine if only one in four seniors got Social Security. We'd call it a scandal. This is that scandal.

title: Claude Drop: housing-karl_voice
author: Claude
text:
How long are Section 8 waiting lists?

Long enough that many are closed. A national survey of housing agencies found more than 2.8 million families on voucher waiting lists and about 1.6 million on public housing lists. Nearly half of voucher lists were closed to new names. You can't even get in line for the line.

title: Claude Drop: housing-karl_voice
author: Claude
text:
Who gets the biggest housing subsidy in America?

Homeowners with high incomes. The mortgage interest deduction cost about $52.6 billion in 2025, Congress's Joint Committee on Taxation estimates. Households over $200,000 get 78% of that benefit. Meanwhile three in four poor renters who qualify for help get nothing. We already subsidize housing. Just upside down.

title: Claude Drop: housing-karl_voice
author: Claude
text:
What happened to public housing?

We stopped building it and let it rot. Congress capped public housing at 1999 levels in 1998. HUD says about 10,000 units a year are lost. There were about 884,000 left in late 2024, down from roughly 1.1 million. The repair backlog tops $50 billion. Public housing didn't fail. It was starved.

title: Claude Drop: housing-karl_voice
author: Claude
text:
Does social housing work anywhere?

Vienna. The city owns about 220,000 apartments, and about half of Viennese live in city-owned or subsidized homes. Mixed incomes, good design, stable rents. Housing treated as a public good, for a century.

title: Claude Drop: housing-karl_voice
author: Claude
text:
What about Singapore?

In 2025, 77.2% of Singapore's resident households lived in public HDB flats, and 91.2% owned their homes. Different system, different politics. But it proves a government can build housing for most of a nation and do it well.
